nodes.summary: `u` and `w` are adjacent (joined by an edge in either direction).
nodes.title: Adjacent vertices in a network structure

nodes.summary: With BDe hyperparameters, a family score is a ratio of set marginal likelihoods.
nodes.title: BDe family score as a ratio of marginal likelihoods

nodes.summary: The Bayesian–Dirichlet score of a family `F` with parent set `P ⊆ F` and hyperparameters `α` on the configurations of `F`.
nodes.title: Bayesian–Dirichlet family score

nodes.summary: The BD score of the structure `Pa` with family hyperparameters `α`: the product of the family scores.
nodes.title: Bayesian–Dirichlet network score

nodes.summary: BDe hyperparameters (Heckerman, Geiger and Chickering): `ess` times the weight `∑_{x ↦ c} p x` of the configuration `c` of `S`. When `∑ x, p x = 1`, `p` is a prior joint distribution and this is the prior probability of `c`.
nodes.title: BDe hyperparameters

nodes.summary: Covered-edge reversal preserves the BDe score (for a positive weight function `p` — a prior when `∑ x, p x = 1` — and positive equivalent sample size).
nodes.title: Covered-edge reversal preserves the BDe score

nodes.summary: Structures connected by a sequence of covered-edge reversals have the same BDe score.
nodes.title: Covered-edge reversals preserve the BDe score

nodes.summary: The BDe score of the structure `Pa`.
nodes.title: BDe network score

nodes.summary: The joint values of the variables in `S`.
nodes.title: Joint configurations of a set of variables

nodes.summary: The number of cases in `D` that take the values `c` on the variables `S`.
nodes.title: Count of cases matching a configuration

nodes.summary: `Pa'` is obtained from `Pa` by reversing a covered edge `x → y` (Chickering 1995): `x` is a parent of `y` and `y`'s other parents are exactly `x`'s parents (`Pa y = insert x (Pa x)`); after the reversal `y` has parents `Pa x` and `x` has parents `insert y (Pa x)`. Acyclicity is not required: the score identity holds for any parent-set maps (on a DAG, `x ∉ Pa x` and `y ∉ Pa x` hold automatically).
nodes.title: Covered-edge reversal

nodes.summary: The structure has no directed cycle.
nodes.title: Acyclic network structure

nodes.summary: `u → w ← z` is a v-structure: two non-adjacent distinct parents of a common child.
nodes.title: V-structure in a directed graph

nodes.summary: The (unnormalized) marginal likelihood of the data restricted to the variables `S` under the BDe Dirichlet prior on the joint values of `S`. `p` is treated as generalized weights here: the total Dirichlet mass over configurations is `ess * ∑ x, p x`, so the omitted normalizing factor is `1 / rising (ess * ∑ x, p x) D.length`, the same for every `S`. When `p` is normalized (`∑ x, p x = 1`) this is…
nodes.title: BDe marginal likelihood of a variable set

nodes.summary: The sequential Pólya–Dirichlet prediction factor for the case `x` after the cases `D`: `∏_v (α_{v,c} + n_{v,c}) / (α_{v,j} + n_{v,j})`, with `c`, `j` the family and parent values of `x` and `n` the counts in `D`. This is a genuine conditional probability only when `Pa` is a DAG; for arbitrary parent maps (e.g. cycles or self-parents) the factors over all cases need not sum to one.
nodes.title: Sequential Pólya–Dirichlet prediction factor

nodes.summary: Chickering's transformational characterization (1995): two acyclic structures with the same skeleton and the same v-structures (Markov equivalent by Verma and Pearl) are connected by a sequence of covered-edge reversals.
nodes.title: Chickering's transformational characterization

nodes.summary: The rising factorial `a (a + 1) ⋯ (a + n - 1)`, equal to `Γ(a + n) / Γ(a)` for `a > 0`.
nodes.title: Rising factorial

nodes.summary: The sequential Pólya–Dirichlet product for the cases `D`, in order, after the cases `E`: each case contributes its `predictive` factor given all cases before it. A genuine probability of the data only when `Pa` is a DAG (see `predictive`).
nodes.title: Sequential Pólya–Dirichlet product after prior cases

nodes.summary: The BD score is the sequential prediction product of the data (hence it does not depend on the order of the cases). This is an identity for all real hyperparameters. Positivity of the hyperparameters only makes every predictive denominator positive; it does not make this product a probability. nodes.title: The BD score is the sequential prediction product

nodes.summary: The sequential Pólya–Dirichlet product for the cases of `D`, in order. A genuine probability of the data only when `Pa` is a DAG (see `predictive`).
nodes.title: Sequential Pólya–Dirichlet product of the data

nodes.summary: The number of cases matching a parent configuration is the sum over the family configurations extending it (`N_j = ∑_k N_jk`).
nodes.title: Parent configuration counts sum over family configurations

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
